summary: Psalm 10 supplies all the evidence. The killer watches for the helpless in verse 8. In verse 14 the helpless entrusts the matter to God, who has been the fatherless child’s helper.

senses.definition: The ambusher watches for a helpless victim. Later the helpless person places his cause in God’s hands beside the fatherless child. The written form in verse 10 can be read as a plural referring to those overpowered.

cognates.note: The comparison supposes an unattested step from darkness to misfortune. The Arabic word gives no direct evidence for the Hebrew social sense.

note: The written חלכאים in verse 10 resembles a plural of this word. The traditional reading divides it into חֵיל כָּאִים. The forms in verses 8 and 14 identify the person by vulnerability without requiring a derivation from darkness.
